reasoning: The claim "lightning never strikes the same place twice" is a well-documented myth. According to the National Weather Service (NWS) and meteorologists, lightning frequently strikes the same location repeatedly, particularly tall, isolated, and pointed objects. This is because these structures provide a path of least resistance for the electrical discharge between the ground and the clouds. For example, the Empire State Building in New York City is struck by lightning an average of 25 times per year.
